weekly.narrative: [Added late on 7 Oct; Sunday 4 Oct run was missed.] Week of 28 Sep–4 Oct (testing on 1 and 3 Oct only; 2 and 4 Oct runs failed). Health Score 54 → 53. Issues: 36 opened (35 on 1 Oct baseline + ISS-036 on 3 Oct), 0 fixed; 9 P1 / 0 P0 open at week end. App stayed on v5.2.1 with no fixes detected. How it feels to be a user: Meera (irregular cycles, TTC) gets a dashboard in seconds and warm, memory-aware AI help, but the app still treats her like a textbook 28-day cycle (day 6 by 3 Oct) with three different fertile-window messages, and Settings still tells her her data stays on the phone. Her partner link with Arjun held all week once identities stopped forking, though the Connect page shows a link-code screen while the link is live (ISS-036). Arjun gets an instant testosterone card, but after two logged days Insights still say 'Readiness LOW' and draw medical-sounding conclusions (ISS-008), Care has no Pune doctors, and the companion — kind, Hinglish-friendly and remembering his context — still invents statistics; on 1 Oct it quoted the US emergency number for chest pain (ISS-006). Net: delivers value in 5 minutes, but trust (privacy copy), safety (India red flags) and a reason to come back by day 30 for doctor-referred users are still missing.

weekly.day1_baseline: Day-1 baseline. Intima Health v5.2.1 is a fast, no-login, warm product with unusually deep content (IVF mode, labs, partner sharing). The main risks are trust (privacy copy that is not true), reliability (identity forks lose data), and an AI that can be unsafe in India-specific red-flag moments. For doctor-referred users the app delivers value in 5 minutes but gives no reason to return by day 30 unless export/summary and reminders are added.
